title: Cross-Stack Standard rule registry
description: The single source of truth for every rule of the Standard. Rule IDs are unique, gates are unique per identity and cross-file references are verified by scripts/check-registry.mjs, which this schema cannot express.

$schema.description: Path or URL of this schema, for editor support.

version.description: Registry format version. It changes only when this schema changes in a way that breaks existing readers.

ruleId.description: Prefix and three digits. Prefixes: BE (Laravel backend), WEB, MOB, SEC, I18N, UI, PROC (process), CI.

enforcement.description: FORCED: enforced structurally, with no known way around it. GUARDED: catches the direct form, and the known evasions are listed. REVIEW: prose only, checked in code review.

line.description: One line of text with no leading or trailing whitespace.

gate.description: The tool check that enforces the rule. id per kind — eslint: rule id; depcruise: rule name; vitest/jest: exact test title; pest: exact test description containing the rule ID; phpstan: error identifier; script: script name; ci: workflow step id or name; hook: hook event name. discriminator per kind — eslint: text that must appear in the enabling config (a selector, import path or message tag); script: sub-check, listed as <id>:<discriminator>; hook: a tool name the event's matcher must cover; ci: the job that holds the step.

allOf.description: A hook gate names a hook event (such as PreToolUse) and, optionally, a tool name its matcher must cover.

discriminator.description: A tool name; MCP tool names carry hyphens from their plugin and server names.

allOf.description: A script gate names a kebab-case script and, optionally, a kebab-case sub-check.
Only eslint, script, ci and hook gates take a discriminator.

title.description: The property as an imperative statement, at most 100 characters and without a trailing period; detail belongs in the summary.

track.description: laravel, web or mobile: that track only. client: both JavaScript client tracks (web and mobile), never Laravel. shared: every project, whatever its tracks.

tier.description: 1: one of the Tier-1 invariants that apply to every project. 2: applies once the project declares Tier 2.

invariant.description: The Tier-1 invariant (1 to 10, in the order of the tier model decision record) the rule belongs to. Required for a tier 1 rule; a tier 2 rule has none.

module.description: The opt-in module the rule belongs to, or null for the track's core.

targetEnforcement.description: The level the rule is being promoted to. Defaults to enforcement. It may be higher than enforcement only while enforcement is REVIEW; the change that ships the gate and both fixtures promotes the rule.

gate.description: Required for FORCED and GUARDED. A REVIEW rule with a higher target may name its planned gate; any other REVIEW rule has null.

evasions.description: Known ways around the gate. Required and non-empty for GUARDED.

decision.description: Number of the architecture decision record the rule follows (docs/decisions/<NNNN>-*.md).

defaultEnabled.description: Whether the rule is on when the project has not configured it; a module rule is on whenever its module is. A default-off rule names its switch (rules.<RULE-ID>.enabled or a module option) in configurable. At a release, a default-on rule must be at its target level (check-registry --release), because promoting a default-on rule later is a MAJOR change.

since.description: The Standard version that first shipped the rule, or, for a rule whose profile or module ships after the current release, the version it is planned for.

configurable.description: Project configuration keys (in .cross-stack/standard.json) that tune or switch the rule. <name> marks a user-chosen segment. A REVIEW rule may name a planned key under trackRoots, stack, decisions, rules or modules before the manifest schema declares it; the change that promotes the rule adds the key.

profiles.description: Web profiles the rule applies to. Omitted means every profile.

summary.description: One sentence that states the rule and what it protects.

adoption.description: One sentence on how an existing project adopts the rule without failing on its first run, starting with one of: Nothing needed (the rule passes as installed or adopt does the work), Fix first (the project changes code or configuration before the check is enabled), Baseline (existing findings go into a shrink-only baseline), Allowlist (existing findings get dated allowlist entries), Opt-in (the rule is off until the project turns it or its module on).

allOf.description: A tier 1 rule names the Tier-1 invariant it belongs to.
Only a tier 1 rule names an invariant.
A GUARDED rule lists at least one known evasion.
A FORCED or GUARDED rule names its gate.
A FORCED rule has no other target; only a REVIEW rule may target a higher level.
A GUARDED rule targets GUARDED; only a REVIEW rule may target a higher level.
A REVIEW rule with no higher target has no gate (null).
Profiles apply only to web-track rules.
